claims.statement: EU battery law requires qualifying EV batteries to expose current state-of-health data in the BMS to lawful purchasers or their agents for residual-value and reuse assessment.

Battery passports become mandatory from 18 February 2027 for relevant newly placed EV batteries and include performance, durability, reuse, and recycling information, so they do not solve near-term coverage of the legacy fleet.
Independent certificate supply is already mature: AVILOO and DEKRA offer rapid model-specific tests, and BCA embeds AVILOO reports in European BEV auctions for EUR 40 per tested vehicle.

The Commission still describes automotive data access as fragmented and potentially needing complementary measures beyond the Data Act, so legal entitlement is not equivalent to a uniform technical interface.

A Poland-first entrant could pilot through licensed diagnostics and dealer partners, but a defensible exchange requires local resale outcomes and transaction integration rather than another standalone certificate.

contrary_evidence: BCA already combines an independent battery report with a large European auction and charges only EUR 40 per report.
AVILOO advertises a EUR 99 retail certificate, below the original 700 PLN certificate hypothesis.
DEKRA and AVILOO have model-specific algorithms and accumulated test databases that a new entrant would initially lack.
Battery-passport and BMS-access rights do not create a uniform interface for the existing used-EV fleet.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot with two to five Warsaw and Wielkopolska EV dealers or diagnostic shops using a licensed test, then seek fleet-lessor batches; the marketplace follows only after repeated certificate-linked sales.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: An unvalidated path requires roughly 15000 annual certificates at about 120 PLN contribution plus exchange fees, or equivalent high-value fleet GMV, before a founder-owned business could plausibly support 5 million PLN of equity in seven to ten years.
economics.founder_time: About 15-20 hours weekly if partner technicians perform tests and the founder limits work to integrations, analytics, and account management.
economics.gross_margin_basis: BCA's EUR 40 report benchmark and AVILOO's EUR 99 retail benchmark imply limited room at 250-500 PLN retail after technician, license, support, and liability costs; margin is unvalidated.
economics.payback: At an unvalidated 100 PLN contribution per certificate, 850 completed certificates recover 85000 PLN of launch capital before founder salary.
economics.pricing: Test 250-500 PLN per vehicle; add a 1-2% transaction fee only where the platform actually sources the buyer.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Fleet disposal and dealer inventory can repeat, but the certificate is purchased once per vehicle and incumbents can be substituted.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Model-specific degradation, certificate, bid, and realized-resale outcomes for the Polish used-EV market
fingerprint.customer: Polish used-EV dealers, fleet lessors, and later battery repurposers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Diagnostic-shop integrations, fleet remarketing contracts, and certificate-linked dealer listings
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Independent licensed battery-health certificate followed by a curated B2B remarketing exchange
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Seller pays when a vehicle is certified; transaction fee applies only when a matched sale closes
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A used EV or pack is remarketed without trusted evidence of remaining capacity and anomalies

founder_fit: Battery analytics fits the founder's data-science and renewable-energy background.
Dealer and diagnostic partners can keep testing physical work bounded and compatible with a full-time job.
Winning fleet accounts and insurer acceptance still requires focused B2B selling, though not a public personal brand.
risks: Incorrect or overstated certificates can create valuation, warranty, and safety liability.
AVILOO, DEKRA, BCA, OEM programs, or another auction can compress price and capture the transaction data.
Unsupported models, inconclusive tests, and proprietary interfaces can interrupt service coverage.
A certificate may improve trust without producing enough incremental sale value to support acquisition cost.

structure.commercial_archetype: Independent inspection certificate plus B2B marketplace
structure.control_point: Battery-health evidence displayed inside the remarketing transaction
structure.critical_dependency: Repeatable model coverage, lawful data access, and dealer adoption at a price competitive with embedded incumbents

thesis: Create a Poland-first independent used-EV battery-health certificate integrated into dealer remarketing, and add a B2B exchange only after certificate-linked sales produce a proprietary local residual-value dataset.
title: Used-EV Battery Health Certificate Exchange
uncertainties: Polish dealers' willingness to pay above embedded European auction pricing is untested.
No evidence yet shows insurers, lenders, or buyers will accept a new certificate methodology.
Supported-model coverage, license cost, test failure rate, and professional-indemnity cost are unknown.
The incremental sale-price or conversion lift in Poland has not been independently measured.
